sets.name: brick_english
sets.notes: Complete photographic scan of true alternating English-bond stretcher/header courses, not a procedural reconstruction. Source coverage is 2.4x1.2 m. Original face chips, lime mortar and measured relief remain co-registered. Native pixel dimensions retained; installer must use the new physical scale.

sets.name: brick_brabant
sets.notes: Photographed red/brown brick, true alternating English bond and co-registered scanned chips/mortar. Lime joint pigment is preserved separately from the restrained warm brick tint. Entire 2.4x1.2 m source scan retained; no short multi-course block repeated.

sets.name: sandstone_ashlar
sets.notes: Scanned limestone/sandstone-coloured ashlar, 2 m coverage, recessed joints and chipped arrises from the same height field. Geometry must round exposed block silhouettes.

sets.name: bluestone_ashlar
sets.notes: Photographed dressed ashlar geometry and grain, adapted to dark grey-blue local stone. Donor is pale sandstone, not an authenticated Belgian quarry scan; fossil identity is not claimed. Mortar and each block retain unique scan detail. Requires geological/art-direction review before acceptance.

sets.name: prison_bluestone
sets.notes: Photographed dressed ashlar geometry and grain, adapted to dark grey-blue local stone. Donor is pale sandstone, not an authenticated Belgian quarry scan; fossil identity is not claimed. Mortar and each block retain unique scan detail. Requires geological/art-direction review before acceptance.

sets.name: stone_petit_granit
sets.notes: Fine photographed dark mineral skin, desaturated to weathered Belgian bluestone colour. Source is a natural rock scan, not a certified petit-granit/fossil specimen. Scanned pits supply real depth. No painted joints across a solid fountain or plinth. Fossil-specific accuracy remains unverified.

sets.name: coping_bluestone
sets.notes: Three 1 m coping blocks, mineral scan with 10-14 mm recessed lime joints. Physical bevelled top and underside remain geometry. No fossil/quarry provenance claimed.

sets.name: slate_ardennes
sets.notes: Photographed overlapping roof slates, 3 m coverage; chipped ends, split grain and laps share measured displacement. Slate colour adapted to grey-blue Ardennes material. Image top is ridgeward; near-visible lips still require geometry.

sets.name: slate_ardennes
sets.notes: Photographed overlapping roof slates, 3 m coverage; chipped ends, split grain and laps share measured displacement. Slate colour adapted to grey-blue Ardennes material. Image top is ridgeward; near-visible lips still require geometry.

sets.name: lead_roof
sets.notes: Retained photographic original lead panels and co-registered structural rolled-seam height. Even grey oxide, no orange rust. Large seam rolls and sheet silhouettes remain geometry.

sets.name: sandstone_plain
sets.notes: Continuous mineral photograph adapted to pale carved sandstone; no block seams on mouldings. Fine measured rock texture only; not a quarry-identification claim.

sets.name: bronze_cast
sets.notes: Photographic original generated bronze pigment; casting micro-pits use scanned metal displacement, with isolated generated pores explicitly reconstructed. Verdigris changes pigment/roughness only. Height is an authored reconstruction, not measured bronze photogrammetry. Base and casting need the same finish; hand-wear and runoff remain localized native work.

sets.name: iron_painted
sets.notes: Retained art2 photographic black-painted iron, granular corrosion, matching authored pits/roughness. No uniform edge-polish mask. Also reused in row 2 and atlas iron cells.

sets.name: zinc_sheet
sets.notes: Photographed fine rolled/pitted metal skin adapted to dull zinc; 0.7 mm total microrelief. Warm steel oxides removed from colour, not turned into zinc rust. No galvanized spangle or oversized painted seams.

sets.name: earth_bare
sets.notes: Continuous photographed soil with real clods, pressed debris and measured displacement. No enlarged circular mud decal. Full donor covers 1.3 m, shared with colour/height/roughness.

sets.name: water_base
sets.notes: Intentional flat absorption colour and flat normal; native animated water supplies reflection and waves. A photographic sky or ripple painted into the base would be incorrect.

sets.name: wood_oak
sets.notes: Photographed weathered boards, fine saw/grain detail, pores and measured joints; full 2 m scan. Grain follows board length. Rotate all maps together on the object; board seams must not cross solid beams.

sets.name: wood_dark
sets.notes: Photographed weathered boards, fine saw/grain detail, pores and measured joints; full 2 m scan. Grain follows board length. Rotate all maps together on the object; board seams must not cross solid beams.

sets.name: barrel
sets.notes: Photographed cask staves and hoops with co-registered measured height; 1.29 m source coverage. Native geometry still owns real hoop/stave thickness and curved silhouette.

sets.name: leather
sets.notes: Photographed brown saddle/upholstery leather, 40 cm scan; creases and fine pore relief kept together. Use model geometry for folds and cut edges.

sets.name: sackcloth
sets.notes: Photographed coarse jute, 269x267 mm source coverage. Thread spacing retained in metre metadata; do not stretch one weave across a full metre.

sets.name: awning_blue
sets.notes: Photographed linen thread relief at about 27 cm per weave tile; original awning pigment, stain and patch layout retained. Four fine-weave repeats per metre are intentional textile structure; no tiled broad stain. Cloth silhouettes and stitched patch edges remain model work.

sets.name: awning_red
sets.notes: Photographed linen thread relief at about 27 cm per weave tile; original awning pigment, stain and patch layout retained. Four fine-weave repeats per metre are intentional textile structure; no tiled broad stain. Cloth silhouettes and stitched patch edges remain model work.

sets.name: tarpaulin
sets.notes: Photographed linen thread relief at about 27 cm per weave tile; original awning pigment, stain and patch layout retained. Four fine-weave repeats per metre are intentional textile structure; no tiled broad stain. Cloth silhouettes and stitched patch edges remain model work.

sets.name: canvas_patched
sets.notes: Photographed linen thread relief at about 27 cm per weave tile; original awning pigment, stain and patch layout retained. Four fine-weave repeats per metre are intentional textile structure; no tiled broad stain. Cloth silhouettes and stitched patch edges remain model work.

sets.name: wood_single
sets.notes: One photographed continuous board, cropped between scan joints; 2 m along grain, 117 mm across. Periodic correction of this crop avoids a visible cut seam. Never apply a multi-board gap across a spoke, beam or solid painted panel.

sets.name: wrought_iron
sets.notes: Retained art2 photographic iron (042db687), with corrosion and aligned authored height. This donor remains suitable; its four maps are compared in the round 2 proof.

sets.name: bark_fissured
sets.notes: Photographed deeply fissured oak plates, full 1x2 m scan, with measured crevices and coarse scales. Generic fissured trunk proxy for lime/elm/willow in existing half-atlas; not a botanical lime scan. Do not stretch to former 0.5x1 m metadata. Species-specific lime accuracy remains a review item.

sets.name: bark_plane
sets.notes: Photographed exfoliating Platanus-family bark, 1.1x2.2 m scan; cream/olive/grey adaptation for Antwerp plane trees. Scanned flake relief stays aligned, broad pigment patches do not create false fissures. Japanese sycamore is the source, not a claim of a London-plane field scan.

sets.name: bark_atlas
sets.notes: Original left/right half rectangles retained. Each half repeats independently. Fissured scan covers 1x2 m; plane scan 1.1x2.2 m. Installer must use per-half metre scales; repeating the entire atlas is invalid.
